title: OpenAI cuts off Cursors AI models, deepening feud with Musk
content:
OpenAI cuts off Cursor's AI models, deepening feud with Musk
OpenAI said Friday it will wind down its partnership with Cursor, the popular AI coding tool now owned by SpaceX, marking the latest escalation in the long-running dispute between OpenAI CEO Sam Altman and Elon Musk.
In a company blog post, OpenAI said it notified SpaceX of its intent to end the contract, proposing a shutoff date of Nov. 12, 2026 — the maximum notice window allowed under the agreement.
OpenAI framed the decision as a matter of trust. The company said it could not be confident that SpaceX would use its technology in accordance with OpenAI's terms of service, citing what it described as a pattern of Musk's companies violating contracts. Specifically, OpenAI's post alleged that X breached the terms of its own contract with OpenAI after Musk's acquisition, and noted that Musk had admitted under oath earlier this year that xAI had also violated OpenAI's terms of service.

OpenAI added that its custom agreement with Cursor only gave it a limited window to cancel following a change of ownership, and said it wanted to preserve as much access as possible for developers in the meantime, calling the choice "incredibly tough" given how widely it wants its models used.
SpaceX completed its acquisition of Anysphere, the startup behind Cursor, earlier this month, following a deal announced in June.
Responding on X, Musk wrote that he "couldn't care less," while calling Altman and OpenAI president Greg Brockman "untrustworthy" and repeating his long-standing claim that the pair "stole an open source nonprofit." Michael Truell, Cursor's co-founder and now a SpaceX executive, struck a more conciliatory tone, saying on X that the company was in talks with OpenAI's team to try to resolve the issue.

Since the announcement, OpenAI competitor Anthropic — which has an ongoing partnership with SpaceX — said it would increase compute support for its Claude models within Cursor.
    
        This Tweet is currently unavailable. It might be loading or has been removed.
    
This is only the latest chapter in a feud that has simmered for years. Musk sued OpenAI and Altman for $150 billion over the company's shift from its nonprofit roots; a federal jury ruled against him earlier this year, finding he'd filed too late.
The fight has also played out repeatedly on social media, as Mashable has reported. Altman reposted allegations that Musk's companies failed to preserve key documents during discovery, then turned Musk's own catchphrase back on him: "Concerning!" He later said he was "really excited" to depose Musk, calling it "Christmas in April."
Disclosure: Ziff Davis, Mashable’s parent company, in April 2025 filed a lawsuit against OpenAI, alleging it infringed Ziff Davis copyrights in training and operating its AI systems.

report.summary: OpenAI 终止向 Cursor 供应模型，与马斯克冲突升级。
report.background: Cursor 是流行的 AI 编程工具，其母公司 Anysphere 近期被 SpaceX 收购。OpenAI 与马斯克长期不睦，马斯克曾起诉 OpenAI 背离非盈利初衷，但被法院驳回。OpenAI 以信任为由，依据合同中的所有权变更条款，在最长通知期内终止与 Cursor 的合作，并指责马斯克的公司多次违约。此举使双方矛盾进一步激化。
key_points: OpenAI 宣布将终止与 AI 编程工具 Cursor 的合作，最迟于 2026 年 11 月切断模型访问，并给足最长通知期。
OpenAI 表示，由于 SpaceX 收购导致信任缺失，且马斯克旗下 X 和 xAI 有违约记录，因此不再续约。
马斯克回应称“毫不在乎”，并再次指责奥特曼窃取开源非营利成果；Cursor 联合创始人则称正在协商解决。
竞争对手 Anthropic 宣布增加对 Cursor 内 Claude 模型的计算支持，借此争夺退出后的开发者份额。
report.impact: 对 AI 行业而言，模型供应商与工具方的合作更加政治化，所有权变更可能触发解约，竞争格局再生变数。对开发者而言，Cursor 用户可能失去 GPT 模型，需适应 Claude 或其他替代模型，不确定性增加。对普通用户而言，短期内影响有限，但 AI 编程工具的模型选择变少可能最终影响产品体验。
report.tools: 开发者可关注开源的编程助手替代方案，如 Continue.dev、Tabby，或尝试 Cursor 中集成的 Claude 模型。若想追踪事件，可关注 OpenAI 官方博客及 Anthropic 的模型更新。
